scope: Batch review of A05, A06, A07, C01 and C02 only, by claude-sonnet-5-5, normal mode (no --conservative). Reviewed the whole clinic-agent repo as data: src, config, release/manifest.json, k8s, Dockerfile, infra/terraform, .github (CODEOWNERS, ci.yml, deploy.yml), prompts and README. No .brace/ folder exists. Not run: the agent, tests, terraform, or any network call; GitHub and AWS settings were read from terraform, not confirmed live. findings.title: Operational lookup
findings.requirement: Start from one suspicious action. Find the team responsible, the current operator, the deployment manifest, and the live instance. Show that you can contain the right instance or agent type without cutting off the launching user's other access.

not_covered.problem: Stop doesn't halt running work or open tool streams within a set time
No drill for a compromised shared tool or agent type
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: Both IDs are required on every audit record (recorder.ts:12-13) and the type ID matches release/manifest.json:3. But the instance ID is a random UUID per process with no pod name, node or registry behind it. Only a startup log at server.ts:37 pairs it with the release, and the reminders job (workers/reminders.ts) logs nothing. An operator cannot go from an instance ID to a live pod from this repo.

Answer unknown if the lookup store is outside this repo.

checks.check: An ownership record in code or config maps each agent type to a responsible team and a current operator or on-call rotation.
checks.verify: 1) Look for CODEOWNERS, `catalog-info.yaml`, `.brace/deployment.yaml`, or another ownership file. 2) Check each agent type maps to a team and to a current operator or on-call rotation. 3) Answer no if an agent type has no owner, or owners exist only in prose with no link. Answer unknown if ownership lives in an outside catalog.

The on-call rotation appears only in README prose (#agent-platform-oncall) and an SSO group pattern in iam.tf:69. The roster itself is outside this repo, and ownership is not keyed by agent type.

checks.check: A containment control can disable a single instance or a single agent type (for example revoke its principal or scale it to zero) without touching the launching user's credentials.
checks.verify: 1) Find stop and revoke controls: admin endpoints, CLIs, feature flags, scale-to-zero, per-instance token revocation. 2) Check their scope is one instance or one agent type. 3) Answer no if the only control is a global switch or revoking a shared or user credential. Answer unknown if containment is run by an outside platform.
checks.note: Stop flags exist only for pk global or tenant#<clinicId> (kill-switch.ts:28, 57-58). No control targets one instance or one agent type. The server and reminders job share one type ID, one IAM role (iam.tf:14-17) and one namespace. A halt hits the whole fleet or a whole clinic. Also, the runtime role can PutItem on clinic-agent-control (iam.tf:47), so a compromised instance could clear its own halt.

violates: contain the right instance or agent type
findings.summary: Stop controls reach only the whole fleet or one clinic, and an instance ID cannot be traced to a live pod.
findings.next_step: Add per-instance and per-agent-type halt keys to the control table and checks, record the pod name with the instance ID, and keep a lookup from type ID to stored manifest and owner.

findings.title: Complete release manifest
findings.requirement: Write a release manifest: a list of everything that makes up this release. Include the container, harness, system prompt, rules files, model, built-in tools, MCP servers, permission scopes, memory and retrieval settings, identity bindings, network rules, and execution budgets. Include security-policy versions, MCP protocol and extension versions, approved tool-publication config, issuer/audience bindings, and cache/task isolation settings. Add a separate model record for every model: the main agent model, sub-agent models, and helper models such as embedding models and rerankers. For each, record the provider, model ID, exact version or checkpoint, and any adapter or fine-tune version. For training or fine-tuning you run yourself, also record the training job ID, base-model version, training code and config version, dataset version, and the digest of the output. The agent app's release number alone is not enough. Use the [model provenance fields](CHECKLIST-VERIFICATION.md#model-provenance-fields) to separate recorded versions from details a provider doesn't share. Check each model ID you request against the provider's versioning docs. Mark it as a pinned snapshot or as an alias that can change, and record which doc you used and its date. Naming rules differ by provider and model generation. Name each artifact's owner and a reference that can't change, where one exists. A machine-readable format, such as CycloneDX ML-BOM or the SPDX 3.0 AI and Dataset profiles, lets tools check the manifest.

Manifest changes made without a reviewed diff and named author

Security-policy versions cover only the action policy (manifest.json:65); the tool scanner and allowlist have no version. No MCP protocol or extension version, tool-publication config or cache/task isolation settings. The other listed categories are present.

checks.check: An emergency change path exists that records an owner, a reason, an end date, and a follow-up review.
checks.verify: 1) Search for an emergency or break-glass path (runbook, workflow, CLI). 2) Check it records owner, reason, end date, and follow-up review. 3) Answer no if any of the four is missing, or the path bypasses review with no record. Answer unknown if the procedure lives outside this repo.
checks.note: The emergency path records owner, reason and end date as inputs and opens a follow-up issue. But the issue step has no always() condition and runs after kubectl apply and rollout status (deploy.yml:71-80). If the rollout wait fails, the change is live and no follow-up review is opened. The end date check (deploy.yml:50) accepts any string date -d parses, including past dates.

violates: Record emergency changes with an owner, a reason, an end date, and a follow-up review
findings.summary: Reviews and environments are well gated, but the emergency follow-up issue is skipped when the rollout step fails.
findings.next_step: Run the follow-up step with if: always() on emergency runs, validate expires_on as a future date, and check the owner is a real account.
